ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The Divine's lotus feet serve as the foundation and refuge for devotees, embodying surrender and shelter. This declaration affirms the central role of the Divine in the lives of the faithful, providing stability and solace. The image conveys a deep sense of dependence and trust. 
Themes: lotus feet, Divine refuge, surrender, shelter, spiritual support, dependence on the Divine, faith, devotion.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
The devotee seeks to focus on the Divine presence, symbolized by lotus feet, representing refuge and surrender, within their heart, relying on the guidance and support of the Perfect Guru. This act of devotion is an expression of commitment to spiritual growth and self-discipline. The devotee is instructed to cultivate this inner connection. 
Themes: lotus feet, Divine presence, refuge, surrender, Perfect Guru, spiritual guidance, inner devotion, self-discipline, naam, simran.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
The Divine's lotus feet symbolize refuge and surrender, inspiring devotion. This passage praises the saints whose minds are imbued with love for the Divine, highlighting their commitment to a life of devotion. It describes a state of being where the love for the Divine is deeply ingrained. 
Themes: devotion, surrender, lotus feet, Divine love, saints, sangat, spiritual commitment, naam.
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥: The Divine Feet serve as a vessel for traversing the worldly ocean, symbolizing refuge and salvation. This image instructs the mind to seek solace in the Divine presence, facilitating spiritual crossing. The stance is advisory, guiding one's own mind towards surrender. Themes: Divine refuge, spiritual crossing, surrender, lotus feet, worldly ocean, salvation, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance).
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
The Divine's lotus feet, a symbol of refuge and surrender, have captivated the mind, rendering all else insipid. This state of being utterly devoted and enamored with the Divine results from the mind being pierced by the Divine presence. The individual is now solely sweetened by the Lord King's presence. 
Themes: Divine presence, lotus feet, refuge, surrender, devotion, naam, worldly detachment, maya's opposite.
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
The individual who has drunk the ambrosial nectar (naam, the divine Name) is satiated and attains a state of immortality, made possible by the Guru's guidance. This declaration asserts the transformative power of spiritual nourishment, rendering one impervious to suffering and mortality. It instructs on the attainment of a timeless state through devotion. 
Themes: immortality, spiritual satiation, Guru's guidance, naam, liberation from suffering, divine nourishment, timeless state, spiritual transformation.
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
The Divine Name's elixir intoxicates those who drink it, freeing them from worldly attachments (maya). This state results from embracing naam (the divine Name) through simran (loving remembrance), shattering the bonds that entangle. Liberation and spiritual ecstasy ensue, as the grip of material ties is broken. 
Themes: spiritual liberation, naam, simran, maya, intoxication, freedom, devotion, spiritual ecstasy
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
The Divine Name is ambrosial nectar that grants spiritual life. This statement praises the one who tastes it, implying a state of spiritual vitality. It instructs the mind to seek this nectar, admonishing it to focus on the Divine. The phrase highlights the life-giving quality of the Lord's Name.

Themes: ambrosial nectar, spiritual life, Divine Name, naam, spiritual vitality, self-refinement, inner nourishment, liberation through remembrance.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
The Divine essence is being urged to be internalized and savored. This is an instruction to cultivate a deeper connection with the Lord through a specific practice, likely naam (the divine Name) or simran (loving remembrance). The tone is advisory, guiding the sangat (the company of the devout) or 'Siblings of Destiny' towards a spiritual practice. 
Themes: Divine essence, spiritual practice, naam, simran, sangat, Sikh spiritual guidance, devotion, Lord's sublime essence.
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
The Divine Name, likened to ambrosial nectar, is poured into one's mouth by the Guru, reviving the soul that was spiritually dead. This statement declares the transformative power of the Guru's guidance and the life-giving effect of the naam. It instructs on the means to attain spiritual rebirth and praises the Guru's role in this process. 
Themes: spiritual rebirth, Guru's guidance, naam, ambrosial nectar, spiritual death, revival, transformation, divine grace.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
The Divine Name (naam) is a treasure trove of spiritual nectar (amrit), offering a life-giving elixir. This declaration invites the devout to gather in the company of the devout (sangat) and partake in this ambrosia through loving remembrance (simran). It instructs and encourages the spiritual aspirant to seek nourishment from the Divine. The statement is both an invitation and a directive to indulge in the divine elixir.

Themes: naam, amrit, spiritual nourishment, sangat, simran, divine elixir, spiritual sustenance, ambrosia
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
The Divine removes the fear of birth and death, ending the cycle of reincarnation, and frees the individual from the cycle of suffering. This declaration asserts the liberating power of the Divine, emphasizing the attainment of a state beyond transmigration. 
Themes: liberation, reincarnation, fearlessness, Divine intervention, cycle of birth and death, moksha (liberation), spiritual freedom, freedom from suffering.
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Attaining a state of intuitive poise and tranquility, one finds the Divine, thereby overcoming the fear of death, specifically the spiritual death that results from ignorance of the Divine. This declaration describes the outcome of a profound spiritual transformation, emphasizing liberation from mortality's fear. 
Themes: intuitive poise, sahaj, Divine union, fearlessness, death, spiritual death, liberation, self-realization.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
Meditating on the divine Word (shabad) dispels the fear of the cycle of birth and death, bringing liberation from the cycle of suffering. This statement instructs on the liberating power of devotion, emphasizing the role of spiritual practice in overcoming existential dread. 
Themes: liberation, spiritual practice, devotion, fear of death, cycle of birth and death, divine Word, shabad, salvation.
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
The Divine is invoked through simran (loving remembrance), freeing one from the cycle of suffering caused by birth, old age, and death. This declaration reassures and instructs, stating that remembrance brings liberation from existential fears. It describes a state of being where one is no longer troubled by the anxieties of life's stages. 
Themes: liberation, simran, existential fear, cycle of birth and death, loving remembrance, freedom from suffering, spiritual reassurance.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
The Divine eradicates suffering from birth and death, ending fear of Yama, the god of death, by being in the company (sangat) of the devout. This statement declares the liberating effect of devotion, instructing that refuge in the Divine brings freedom from worldly suffering. It admonishes one's own mind to seek this refuge. 
Themes: liberation, freedom from suffering, sangat, Yama, fearlessness, divine refuge, birth and death cycle, worldly attachment (maya)
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
Fearlessness results from spiritual progress, as the cycle of rebirth (janam maran) is transcended. This declaration asserts liberation from existential dread, signifying a profound transformation. The subject is freed from the anxieties of repeated birth and death, attaining a state of fearlessness and spiritual emancipation. 
Themes: liberation, fearlessness, rebirth, spiritual progress, existential dread, emancipation, cycle of life and death, transcendence.
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Embracing the sangat (the company of the devout), one cultivates love for the Divine, fostering a deep connection. This connection is facilitated by the supportive community, which enables the individual to develop a profound affection. The sangat serves as a catalyst for this spiritual bonding. 
Themes: sangat, community support, divine love, spiritual connection, love for the Divine, communal devotion.
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
Being in the sangat (the company of the devout) enables one to transcend the world-ocean (the cycle of rebirth driven by maya, worldly attachment), thereby severing the noose of death (the cycle of mortality). This statement instructs on the liberating role of communal spiritual practice. It declares that associating with the holy leads to spiritual liberation and freedom from the fear of death. 
Themes: spiritual liberation, sangat, world-ocean, cycle of rebirth, maya, noose of death, mortality, communal spiritual practice.
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Being part of the sangat (the company of the devout) leads to union with the Divine. This statement declares the outcome of joining a community of spiritual seekers. It instructs on the importance of communal spiritual practice for achieving a personal connection with the Divine. 
Themes: sangat, community, spiritual union, Divine connection, collective practice, union with God, sacred assembly, spiritual growth.
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
The devotees are immersed in the sangat (the company of the devout), perpetually united with the divine, and overflowing with love; they sing the praises of the Divine. This passage is praising the state of being deeply connected to the divine community and celebrating the joy of devotion. It describes a state of spiritual ecstasy and unity. 
Themes: Sangat, divine love, devotion, simran (loving remembrance), spiritual ecstasy, community, union with the divine, celestial love.
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ: The Divine lifts humans out of vice and corruption by engaging their minds in the sangat (the company of the devout), thereby detaching them from worldly attachments. This statement declares the transformative power of the devout community, highlighting its role in spiritual redemption and the redirection of one's focus. It underscores the idea that spiritual growth occurs through communal devotion and the abandonment of corrupting influences. Themes: spiritual redemption, sangat, detachment from maya, divine intervention, spiritual growth, community, vice, corruption.
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
The Divine is glorified through sangat (the company of the devout), highlighting the importance of gathering with the spiritually enlightened. This statement is an instruction to heed the value of such assembly. It emphasizes the transformative power of communal spiritual practice, encouraging listeners to acknowledge and appreciate its significance. 
Themes: sangat, community, spiritual growth, Divine glory, gurusangat, assembly, enlightenment, transformation
ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
The Divine is the source of all comfort and peace, embodied in the Guru. This declaration affirms the Guru's role as a bringer of solace and tranquility, identifying the Guru with the ultimate reality, Paramesar (the Supreme Being). It expresses a state of profound trust and surrender. 
Themes: Guru as Paramesar, source of peace, comfort, spiritual solace, divine embodiment, surrender, trust.
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
The Divine is the creator, sustainer, and benefactor of all beings, embodying the roles of originator, omnipresent force, and generous provider. This declaration affirms the Divine's multifaceted nature, emphasizing its comprehensive involvement in the lives of all creatures. 
Themes: creator, sustainer, provider, omnipresence, divine generosity, cosmic architect, universal benefactor, all-pervading force.
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
The Divine is invoked as the embodiment of compassion and kindness, a treasure trove of mercy, and is entreated to grant darshan (spiritual vision or glimpse of the Divine). The granting of darshan is associated with bestowing a redeemed or elevated state of spiritual life. This invocation is a plea for spiritual upliftment through the Divine's gracious presence.

Themes: compassion, kindness, mercy, darshan, spiritual redemption, divine grace, spiritual vision, elevated spiritual state
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
The Divine is praised as the embodiment of virtues and profound depth, emphasizing its richness and complexity. This statement is a declaration of the Divine's qualities, highlighting its excellence and capacity. 
Themes: Divine virtues, profound nature, excellence, richness, qualities of the Divine, depth of character.
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
The Divine is the ultimate provider and generous giver; this declaration acknowledges the impossibility of adequately praising such a being. It is a statement of humility and awe, recognizing the limitations of human expression in the face of divine benevolence. The speaker is effectively admonishing their own mind to acknowledge its own incapacity. 
Themes: divine generosity, impossibility of praise, humility, awe, limitations of human expression, provider, giver, naam (the divine Name)
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
The Divine is praised for being the treasure of all excellence and virtues, emphasizing the impossibility of recounting all its attributes. This expression of devotion acknowledges the Divine as the ultimate source and sustainer of all qualities. It is a statement of surrender and admiration, highlighting the richness of the Divine's nature. 
Themes: divine virtues, praise, devotion, surrender, excellence, sustenance, naam (the divine Name), divine attributes.
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
The Divine will not tolerate worldly attachment (maya) for even an instant, warning the individual consumed by it. This statement admonishes one's own mind, declaring the inevitability of being cast out from the shelter of the Divine presence, symbolized by the home or household. It underscores the urgency of letting go of attachment. 
Themes: divine justice, impermanence, maya, worldly attachment, transience, divine presence, household as refuge.
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
The Divine is the fulfiller of desires, so the mind should trust and not waver. This statement is a reassurance and an admonishment to the mind to have faith. It instructs the mind to be still, as its desires are being met by the Lord. The stance is one of calming the mind's doubts.
Themes: faith, trust, stillness, Divine fulfillment, mind's wavering, kama (desire), man (mind), paramatma (the Supreme Being)
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
The instruction is to meditate on the Lord of the Universe (Gobind), urging the mind to engage in devotion and remembrance. This is an admonishment to one's own mind to adopt a devotional stance, emphasizing the importance of spiritual practice. The mind is being counseled to focus on the divine.

Themes: devotion, meditation, remembrance, spiritual practice, Gobind (the Lord of the Universe), naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), inner reflection.
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
The Divine, the treasure of all joys, resides within; instructing the mind to cease external searching and look inward. This statement admonishes one's own mind to redirect its quest for fulfillment from outside to its inner self, emphasizing the presence of the ultimate reality within. 
Themes: inner Divine presence, introspection, cessation of external search, self-realization, naam (the divine Name) within, spiritual introspection, inner refuge.
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
The speaker admonishes the mind, addressing it as a madman consumed by worldly attachment (maya), urging it to listen and heed the warning. The mind has gone astray by being distracted by worldly allurements. The speaker is instructing the mind to refocus and not be swayed by external attractions. 
Themes: worldly attachment, distraction, spiritual waywardness, mindfulness, divine guidance, heedlessness, maya, spiritual correction
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥: Attain humility by becoming the dust under the feet of those devoted to simran (loving remembrance), thereby surrendering to their spiritual stature. This instruction emphasizes the importance of reverence and self-abasement in the pursuit of spiritual growth. It advises adopting a stance of devotion and humility. Themes: humility, surrender, simran, devotion, spiritual growth, reverence, self-abasement.
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
The Divine grants countless royal delights when the True Guru (spiritual guide) bestows a gracious glance, signifying spiritual awakening and enlightenment. This statement praises the Guru's role in revealing the divine, instructing on the path to spiritual joy. 
Themes: spiritual guidance, divine grace, enlightenment, True Guru, spiritual joy, mystical experience, naam (the divine Name) revelation, guru-disciple relationship.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
The Divine's mercy, embodied in the True Guru, transforms one's perception of suffering, rendering it unrecognizable as pain. This declaration asserts the liberating effect of the Guru's compassion, redefining the experience of hardship. It instructs that with the Guru's blessing, one transcends the conventional understanding of pain. 
Themes: Guru's compassion, transformation of suffering, liberation, divine mercy, perception of pain, spiritual transcendence.
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ: The Divine is attained in the fourth stage of spiritual union, marked by profound peace and stillness (sahaj) in the mind. This state is one of surrender and devotion, where the individual self is subsumed by the divine presence, embodied in the image of the marriage ceremony. The attainment is a result of divine grace, not human effort. Themes: spiritual union, sahaj (inner peace), divine attainment, surrender, devotion, marriage ceremony as spiritual metaphor, self-subsumption, divine grace.
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
The Divine is pleased when the True Guru is cherished in the heart, resulting in the attainment of peace and fulfillment. This statement instructs on the means to achieve a state of contentment by internalizing the Guru's guidance. 
Themes: peace, True Guru, satguru (the true spiritual guide), inner fulfillment, spiritual guidance, heart, devotion, surrender.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
The Divine preceptor, embodied in the True Guru, provides unwavering support and liberates from suffering by eradicating its root cause, symbolized as cutting the 'banner of pain' or the 'boodi wala tara' (the malignant star). This declaration of reliance and deliverance is a statement of refuge and surrender. It asserts the Guru's role in spiritual emancipation. 
Themes: True Guru, spiritual liberation, refuge, suffering, surrender, divine support, emancipation, Guru's role.
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
The text urges the individual to seize the present opportunity to attain union with the Divine, referred to as Gobind (the Lord of the Universe). It is an exhortation, admonishing one's own mind to make the most of this chance. The statement declares the significance of human life as a means to achieve a spiritual goal. 
Themes: spiritual opportunity, Divine union, self-reflection, Gobind, spiritual attainment, human purpose, divine meeting, chance for enlightenment
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
Human life is purposeful, aimed at gaining spiritual profit through acquiring the divine Name (naam). This statement instructs, emphasizing the potential for growth and the importance of utilizing life's opportunity. It admonishes one's own mind to focus on the true purpose. The idea is that life is for spiritual gain, earning a valuable return, and accumulating inner wealth. 
Themes: spiritual profit, divine Name, human purpose, life's opportunity, inner wealth, naam, worldly vs spiritual gain.
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
The Divine's devotional worship is firmly established within by meeting the guru (a spiritual guide or saintly being), thereby strengthening one's spiritual practice. This instruction emphasizes the importance of associating with the enlightened to deepen one's connection with the Divine. It advises on a path to spiritual growth and self-realization. 
Themes: sangat (the company of the devout), guru, spiritual growth, self-realization, devotion, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), spiritual practice.
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
The human life is fulfilled when one listens to and continually practices the remembrance of the Divine (simran), attaining a state of eternal existence. This statement is a declaration of the purpose of human life, emphasizing the importance of devotion to achieve a lasting spiritual state. It praises the life of one who engages in loving remembrance. 
Themes: fruitful life, remembrance of the Divine (simran), eternal existence, devotion, spiritual fulfillment, naam, meditation on the Lord.
ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
The speaker yearns to obtain the dust from the feet of saintly people (sant jana), applying it to their forehead as a mark of devotion and humility, signifying refuge and surrender. This act is a declaration of their stance of reverence and seeking spiritual guidance. 
Themes: spiritual humility, devotion, saintly company (sangat), refuge, surrender, spiritual guidance, self-abasement, reverence.
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
The Divine is entreated to grant the dust of the feet of Guru's Sikhs (devout followers), an image of humility and spiritual purification, to attain a higher spiritual state. This plea for spiritual upliftment is a statement of one's own unworthiness and a desire for liberation from sin. It is a supplication for salvation through association with the devout (sangat). 
Themes: spiritual purification, humility, liberation from sin, sangat, divine grace, salvation, self-abasement, spiritual upliftment.
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
The speaker expresses devotion to humble devotees, applying the dust from their feet to their face, signifying reverence and a desire to be in their company. This act is a statement of surrender and a longing to be part of the sangat (the company of the devout). The speaker is seeking to connect with the divine through the community of devotees. 
Themes: sangat, humility, reverence, surrender, devotion, community, spiritual connection, divine presence
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
The speaker humbly commits to serving a devotee of the Divine, wiping their feet with their own hair as an act of devotion and surrender, illustrating the value of selfless service and reverence for those who are devoted to the Lord. This act symbolizes the speaker's own devotion and willingness to take a subservient role. 
Themes: selfless service, seva, surrender, devotion, humility, reverence, sangat, spiritual humility, service to the devotee.
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
The supplicant yearns for the bliss that comes from being blessed with the dust of the feet of the saints, an image of humility and surrender to the divine presence. This plea for divine grace is a declaration of one's own insufficiency and a longing for spiritual peace. The act of seeking the dust of the saints' feet is a metaphor for seeking refuge and spiritual guidance. 
Themes: divine grace, humility, surrender, spiritual peace, sangat (the company of the devout), refuge, longing, naam (the divine Name) through association with saints.
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
The supplicant yearns for total surrender to the saints, seeking to humble themselves by touching their feet with their forehead, gazing upon their divine presence, and being covered in the dust of their feet. This plea is a declaration of devotion, expressing a deep longing to be in the presence of the enlightened. 
Themes: surrender, devotion, humility, sangat (the company of the devout), spiritual longing, self-abasement, divine presence.
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
The Divine is supremely beautiful and captivating, beloved by all, yet remains distinct and separate from all. This declaration praises the Divine's unique presence, emphasizing both its pervasiveness and transcendence. It invokes a sense of reverence and wonder, highlighting the Divine's otherworldly beauty. 
Themes: divine beauty, transcendence, immanence, spiritual presence, mysticism, divine love, naam (the divine Name)
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
The Divine's essence, form, and loving presence are profoundly beautiful, inspiring devotion and admiration. This declaration praises the beauty of the Divine, emphasizing its captivating and endearing qualities, and is a statement of reverence and surrender to the Lord's beauty. 
Themes: beauty of the Divine, naam (the divine Name), divine form, loving presence, devotion, admiration, reverence, surrender.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
The Divine is being praised for its beauty and its role as the source of all sweetness and nourishment, embodying the qualities of being aesthetically pleasing and life-sustaining. This statement is an expression of admiration and reverence, highlighting the Divine's capacity to delight and nurture.

Themes: beauty, Divine, source, nourishment, sweetness, admiration, reverence, aesthetic pleasure, life sustenance.
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The speaker is utterly enamored with the Divine, describing it as captivating and beautiful. This declaration conveys the speaker's state of being completely enthralled and surrendered. The speaker's mind is absorbed in the Divine presence, illustrating the intense longing and love. The speaker is instructing their own mind or declaring their experience.

Themes: Divine beauty, longing, love, surrender, spiritual intoxication, enamorment, mystical experience, devotion.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
The Divine, revered as the merciful Lord (Gopal) of the universe, radiates beauty and glory, embodying boundless and infinite splendor. This declaration extols the majesty and limitless nature of the Divine, affirming its supreme status. It conveys a state of reverence and awe, describing the Divine's glory as both beautiful and infinite.
Themes: divine glory, infinite splendor, Gopal (the Divine as protector), mercy, boundless nature, reverence, divine majesty, beauty.
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
The Divine safeguards its devotees' honour, prompting them to remember the divine Name (naam), thereby fostering a state of devotion and protection. This declaration underscores the reciprocal relationship between the Divine and its servants, where the Divine's preservation enables remembrance. 
Themes: divine protection, remembrance, naam, simran, devotion, reciprocal relationship, safeguarding honour, servant-divine dynamic.
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
The Divine safeguards the honor of devotees, consistently protecting them across ages, underscoring a timeless commitment to their dignity and well-being. This declaration affirms the Divine's enduring role as a guardian and protector, emphasizing trust and security in devotion. 
Themes: Divine protection, safeguarding honor, devotees, timeless commitment, trust, security, devotion, protection across ages.
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
The Divine is the cherished Lord of the devotees' lives and is dearly loved by them in return, embodying a mutual affection. This statement affirms the reciprocal love between the devotees and the Divine, highlighting the intimate relationship. It declares the Divine as both the object and subject of love, fostering a deep sense of connection and devotion. 
Themes: mutual love, devotion, Divine as Beloved, reciprocal affection, love for the Divine, devotee-Divine relationship.
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
The Divine is the refuge and sustenance of its devotees and saints, embodying the role of a creator and supporter. This declaration affirms the Divine's role in sustaining the faithful, emphasizing reliance and shelter. It establishes the Divine as the foundation for those devoted to it. 
Themes: divine support, refuge, creator, sustenance, devotion, shelter, naam, saints, devotees.
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
The Divine creates devotees in every era and protects their honor, illustrating a timeless relationship between the Lord and the faithful. This declaration affirms the Lord's consistent support and preservation of those devoted to Him, emphasizing trust and refuge. 
Themes: Divine devotion, protection, honor, timeless relationship, Lord's support, faithfulness, preservation, refuge in the Divine.
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
The speaker implores the Divine Master to disregard their karma (actions and their consequences) and instead protect the honor of their servant. This plea is a statement of humility and surrender, acknowledging the speaker's inadequacy and the Master's authority. The speaker is seeking refuge and salvation. 
Themes: surrender, refuge, karma, Divine mercy, honor, servitude, salvation, protection
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
The supplicant who continually asks for the divine Name (naam) is accepted by the Master, who grants their request. This statement instructs and reassures, declaring the efficacy of persistent devotion and the benevolence of the Divine. It describes a state of receptivity and response between the devotee and the Master. 
Themes: devotion, supplication, divine Name, naam, acceptance, Master's benevolence, receptivity, spiritual request, surrender.
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
The speaker yearns for the divine Name (naam), seeking contentment and an end to their mind's craving. This plea is a declaration of dependence on the Divine for inner peace. By asking for the Name, the speaker is seeking refuge and surrender. The request is for a state of satisfaction that quenches the mind's hunger. 
Themes: divine Name, contentment, inner peace, craving, surrender, spiritual longing, satisfaction, refuge.
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
The speaker, a humble supplicant, repeatedly implores the Divine for the gift of naam (the divine Name), acknowledging their dependence on the Almighty. This plea conveys a stance of surrender and longing. The speaker is instructing their own mind to persist in devotion, emphasizing the importance of seeking the Divine.

Themes: naam, supplication, surrender, devotion, longing, divine dependence, spiritual seeking.
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
The speaker implores the Divine, addressed as Gopal (the sustainer of the world) and Gobind (the lord of the universe), to show mercy and facilitate the remembrance of the divine Name (naam). This plea is a surrender, seeking refuge in the Divine's benevolence to enable a devotional practice. The speaker is instructing their own mind to seek help from the Divine. 
Themes: divine mercy, remembrance of naam, surrender, devotion, plea for assistance, loving remembrance (simran), refuge in the Divine.
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
The speaker, a supplicant, requests a gift from the Divine, their Beloved, seeking spiritual wealth. This plea is an expression of humility and recognition of one's dependence on the Divine. The act of begging signifies the speaker's acknowledgment of their own spiritual poverty. 
Themes: spiritual poverty, divine gift, humility, supplication, naam (the divine Name), spiritual wealth, longing, dependence on the Divine.
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
The speaker, acknowledging their own humility and need, requests divine mercy and charity, surrendering to the Divine presence at their "door". This plea is an act of devotion, recognizing the Divine as the source of all gifts. The speaker is seeking refuge and benevolence. 
Themes: divine mercy, surrender, devotion, refuge, charity, humility, begging, Divine presence.
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
Receiving even a drop of naam (the divine Name) causes the mind to flourish and the body to become spiritually vibrant, signifying a state of spiritual rejuvenation and inner growth. This declaration highlights the transformative power of connecting with the divine. 
Themes: spiritual rejuvenation, naam, inner growth, divine connection, spiritual flourishing, mystical nourishment.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
Drinking in the divine Name's elixir, one becomes forever saturated with its essence, illustrating the transformative power of naam (the divine Name). This statement declares the enduring effect of spiritual communion, where the individual is dyed in the colour of the divine, signifying a profound and lasting change. 
Themes: divine Name, naam, spiritual transformation, elixir, saturation, colouration, spiritual communion, mystical union.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
The Divine is praised through kirtan (congregational devotional singing), the ambrosial (life-giving) essence, yielding unbroken, blissful resonance within. This practice sustains a state of spiritual ecstasy, day and night. It instructs the devotee to prioritize kirtan, promising an enduring, joyful connection with the Divine. 
Themes: kirtan, naam (divine Name), spiritual ecstasy, inner bliss, devotion, Naad (spiritual sound current), spiritual practice, self-surrender.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
The speaker exhorts their tongue to drink in the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name), urging it to savor the spiritual elixir that grants eternal life. This is an instruction to engage in simran (loving remembrance), to relish the divine presence. The tongue is being admonished to focus on the spiritual sustenance. 
Themes: naam, simran, spiritual nourishment, divine elixir, tongue, remembrance, ambrosial nectar, self-discipline.
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
The devotee is utterly absorbed in the divine Name (naam), reveling in its joy and ecstasy, and is surrendered to the Divine presence. This state of being is one of profound spiritual intoxication, where the devotee's individual identity is subsumed by the experience of the divine essence. The devotee is praising the Divine and describing their own state of devotion.

Themes: divine Name, spiritual intoxication, devotion, surrender, ecstasy, naam, loving remembrance, simran, self-transcendence, mystical experience.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
The Divine Name is savored through the Guru's guidance, yielding a life-giving elixir. This experience inspires selfless devotion, surrendering one's being to the Naam. The speaker is instructed on the means to attain spiritual sustenance and is admonishing their own mind to prioritize this pursuit. 
Themes: naam, gurmukh (Guru-oriented), simran, spiritual nourishment, self-sacrifice, surrender, ambrosial essence, divine love.
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
The speaker yearns for the divine Name (naam), the essence that gives spiritual life, and asks how to attain it. This inquiry reflects a longing to experience the sublime and ambrosial nature of the divine. The speaker is seeking a way to taste this essence, indicating a desire for spiritual nourishment. The inquiry is a plea for guidance on accessing the divine.

Themes: divine Name, spiritual longing, ambrosia, naam, spiritual nourishment, divine attainment, yearning, spiritual guidance.
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
The speaker admonishes their companion to abandon the dull, unfulfilling experience of worldly indulgences (vikhiai, worldly corruption or sensual pleasures) and instead savor the sublime, life-giving essence of naam (the divine Name). This is an instruction to prioritize spiritual nourishment over fleeting, unsatisfying worldly delights, seeking refuge in the divine. 
Themes: spiritual nourishment, naam, worldly corruption, vikhiai, sensual pleasures, maya, divine refuge, spiritual discipline.
